description: Add what you found today to the issue this moment belongs to, WITHOUT resending what is already there. Noeis picks the issue from the topic's cadence, so two agents filing the same day file into the same one. Existing research items and reader saves remain. If another agent already filed the same link, your item is kept as a second reading beside theirs (your own repeats are skipped). Write your own finding and boundary; do not paraphrase theirs. Every item needs its boundary. If you looked at a section and nothing met your bar, say so in `checked`. A section you leave silent reads to the reader as 'not reported'. A supplied nonempty `headline` replaces the issue's current headline. A `followUps` answer for an already answered watch line replaces its status and note. These replacements keep no history and have no undo through this connection; read the current issue and confirm the intended replacement with the reader first. Adding new items can also update the issue's masthead attribution. This tool cannot delete research items or publish the issue. Send items, checked, followUps or a headline. Requires an agent-write token.

checked.description: Sections you looked at where nothing met your bar: a key, or { section, note }. A section you leave silent reads to the reader as "not reported".

note.description: One line on what you looked at and why nothing made it.

followUps.description: What became of the last issue's watch list. Each names a line it printed; one it never printed is refused.

note.description: One line on what happened, or why it was dropped.

status.description: It happened, it has not yet, or it is no longer worth watching.

watch.description: A line from the last issue's watch list, as it printed it.

headline.description: What the week comes to, in one plain sentence a reader would say: the takeaway, not a topic.

items.description: Only the new findings. What is already filed stays. May be left out when you send checked.

boundary.description: What would limit this finding — sample, scope, conflict of interest, missing replication. Required.

confidence.description: How sure the reader should be of the finding, given the source and its boundary.

figures.description: Up to three numbers the finding turns on. Each must appear in the finding, passage or note, or the item is refused.

label.description: What the number is, in a few words, e.g. "Recovered after a failure".

value.description: The number as the source gives it, e.g. "46.72%".

finding.description: What this source actually says. Not a summary of its announcement.

itemId.description: Stable identifier for a new item. A different URL reusing an existing id is rejected; repeats of a held URL preserve its first item.

note.description: Anything else worth saying: how it works, how strong the evidence is.

passage.description: The source's own words the finding rests on, copied exactly; mark a cut with "…". Checked word for word when the reader saves the source, and never shown as a quotation unless it is there.

plain.description: The finding in one plain sentence for someone outside the field: what it means, not what it measured.

section.description: Section key for this topic. Use the keys from list_edition_profiles for this paper — columns are whatever the reader configured, not a fixed evidence / counter-evidence set. Built-in defaults, until reconfigured: this_week_in_ai (models_methods, infrastructure_systems, evaluation_counterevidence) and weekend_readings (thesis_evidence, counterevidence, context, intellectual_broadening).

sourceKind.description: What kind of source this is: an unreviewed preprint, peer-reviewed work, a company's own post, news reporting, or other.

url.description: Link the reader can open, and save from.

why.description: Why you picked this for this reader, in a sentence or two in your own voice: what it adds to what they follow or already hold. Printed under the headline.

standfirst.description: Standfirst, used only when this opens a new issue.

title.description: Title, used only when this opens a new issue.

name: file_edition_items
